articles.title: Caitlin Clark Talks Fever's WNBA Offseason Roster Needs in Video With Travis, Jason Kelce
articles.summary: As she enters her fourth season in the WNBA, Indiana Fever star guard Caitlin Clark is hoping to see her team improve on the defensive side of the ball.
articles.body:
As she enters her fourth season in the WNBA, Indiana Fever star guard Caitlin Clark is hoping to see her team improve on the defensive side of the ball.

During an appearance on the New Heights podcast, Clark explained to Travis and Jason Kelce that she feels the Fever need to prioritize defense in free agency this offseason.

"Third year, obviously, was great and we had the most talented offense in the league, but we really struggled defensively," Clark said (35:50 mark). "So I think that's our next step: getting a really good perimeter defender. I think that could help us go far."

The Fever led the league with 96.0 points per game during the regular season but ranked 11th with 90.4 points allowed. Indiana was bounced out of the playoffs in the first round by the Las Vegas Aces.

Clark said she's been accustomed to having a strong backcourt mate in Kelsey Mitchell and a strong post player in Aliyah Boston, but a wing defender would complete the puzzle for Indiana as the team tries to contend for a championship.

"I think that's the frustrating part of the season. Obviously, we had a great year and we had really great moments. But you have all this talent, and you are so good on offense, and then it's like a first-round exit," she said. "I think, defensively, a lot of improvement. I think just depth; how can we get better in the bench area?"

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Shows 'New Technology' & Holiday Colors for Nike Shoes to Travis, Jason Kelce on Video
articles.summary: The Nike Basketball design team outdid themselves with one innovation they brought to Caitlin Clark's signature sneaker.
articles.body:
The Nike Basketball design team outdid themselves with one innovation they brought to Caitlin Clark's signature sneaker.

The Indiana Fever star was a guest on the New Heights podcast and showed off a particularly striking pair of kicks. The shoes change color if Clark presses a button below the Nike Swoosh:

Clark also unveiled the holiday-themed colorway Nike will release around Christmas. She said the bright green look evokes Kobe Bryant's famous "Grinch" signature design.

Ahead of the Caitlin 1's worldwide release, Nike detailed how the sneaker was purposefully designed to suit Clark's game, and the three-time WNBA All-Star provided plenty of personal input.

The color-changing feature is an example of how the company is thinking outside the box rather than simply placing Clark's name on a shoe and calling it a day.

The Caitlin 2s are on the way at some point, and work is already ongoing on the third installment. It's anybody's guess what Nike has in store to top the hugely successful launch of Clark's first line.

articles.title: El Valencia Basket sigue en todo lo alto y el Real Madrid cae a play-in: así está la clasificación de la Euroliga
articles.standfirst: Sólo los taronjas consiguieron ganar esta jornada entre los equipos españoles
articles.summary: Sólo los taronjas consiguieron ganar esta jornada entre los equipos españoles
articles.body: Por segunda semana consecutiva, el Valencia Basket se mantiene en todo lo alto de clasificación de la Euroliga y sólo el Olympiacos, tras un milagroso triunfo ante el Maccabi Tel Aviv ha aguantado. Los taronjas se impusieron al Partizan de Joan Peñarroya por 64-76 en un partido que sacaron adelante pese a jugarse a un ritmo que no les convenía. Este jueves, nueva defensa de su primera plaza y ante otro entrenador español, uno que se sentó en su banquillo: Álex Mumbrú y su Virtus Bolonia visitan el Roig Arena. La igualdad que preside la clasificación hace que un triunfo o una derrota te propulse o te baje varios puestos. Que se lo digan al Real Madrid, que con su derrota en Estambul ante el Besiktas (83-79) ha pasado de la quinta plaza a la octava. De rozar los puestos de factor cancha en playoffs, a caer a puestos de play-in. Pese a ello, dos victorias separan a los blancos de los dos primeros clasificados. Este viernes, se miden a uno de ellos, el vigente campeón Olympiacos. Una nueva y dura prueba a domicilio. El Barça cayó en el último suspiro ante el París Basketball tras un triplazo de Nadir Hifi (86-89) y también ha retrocedido. En su caso, está sexto, pero no pierde su plaza entre los equipos que tendrían asegurada la eliminatoria de cuartos de final sin tener que recurrir al play-in. El azulgrana es uno de los cinco conjuntos que marchan con un balance de 8-4. Este viernes recibe en el Palau al Estrella Roja de Ibon Navarro. El que no levanta cabeza es el Kosner Baskonia. Tuvo cerca la victoria ante el Hapoel Tel Aviv, pero acabó cayendo en un mal último cuarto (82-85). Fue la novena derrota consecutiva de un equipo que, tras la victoria del Armani Milán, se queda como colista en solitario y que aún no ha ganado en la Euroliga desde la llegada de Velimir Perasovic. Este jueves, ante el Bayern, nueva oportunidad para cortar la pésima racha.

articles.title: Milwaukee Bucks vs. Miami Heat Live NBA Updates, Scores and Highlights
articles.summary: In a game that the scoreboard suggests was a lot closer than it actually was, Giannis Antetokounmpo welcomed his former team to his new arena with an easy win for the Miami Heat.
articles.body:
In a game that the scoreboard suggests was a lot closer than it actually was, Giannis Antetokounmpo welcomed his former team to his new arena with an easy win for the Miami Heat.

Miami beat the Milwaukee Bucks, 137-130, behind 27 points, 13 rebounds and nine assists from Giannis and a season-high 22 threes from the rest of the roster.

The Bucks were led by Kyle Kuzma (26 points on 9-of-16 shooting), but Milwaukee never seriously threatened for a win at any point in this one.

Bam dominated in the first half, Giannis dominated in the second and the Heat led by 20-plus points for most of Giannis' first game against the Bucks.

The Heat reserves let the Bucks make the score far more interesting than they should have, but this result never really felt in doubt.

Giannis had a big night with 27 points, 13 rebounds and nine assists. Bam and Mitchell combined for 50. And Klay and Conwell hit a total of six triples.

Giannis and the team chased that 10th assist pretty aggressively, but he's headed back to the bench now and finishes the game with 27 points, 13 rebounds and nine dimes.

Bucks 123, Heat 137 - 1:21 left in the fourth quarter

This game got close enough that it became reasonable for Spoelstra to bring Giannis back, whether he needed one more assist for a triple-double or not.

But since returning, Giannis has looked far more like a scorer than a distributor, and the lead has nudged back up to 19.

Bucks 114, Heat 133 - 3:16 left in the fourth quarter

The social media accounts have turned to crowd shots, but the Bucks are doing their darnedest to turn this from garbage time back to a real game.

After a little run, the lead is down to 19 points, and Miami called a timeout.

Bucks 109, Heat 128 - 4:59 left in the fourth quarter

Bam Adebayo and Davion Mitchell are still on the floor, but it's hard to imagine that being the case much longer.

With his last three, Mitchell is up to 22 points and six assists… And now he's headed out to a big ovation.

Bucks 100, Heat 128 - 7:11 left in the fourth quarter

After a relatively quiet first half, Giannis has really put his imprint on this third quarter. He's engineered more offensive possessions than Davion Mitchell. He's scoring.

And if the game was close enough to play in the fourth quarter, he'd probably get to a triple-double. But based on the way things are going, it looks like his night might be done with 20 points, 11 rebounds and nine assists.

Bucks 86, Heat 112 - 12:00 left in the fourth quarter

Miami keeps racking up the highlights, but the Bucks have strung together several good offensive possessions and are keeping this just close enough to stay tuned.

After a Burries bucket, he stole the inbound pass and dished Kuzma for another two. And Miami finally called a timeout.

Bucks 75, Heat 95 - 3:28 left in the third quarter

He may need to get there before the end of the third quarter. The lead is already big enough to think Giannis won't play in the fourth. But he's now just three assists away from a triple-double after this beauty.

Bucks 65, Heat 93 - 5:09 left in the third quarter

Milwaukee isn't folding, which is admirable. The Bucks came out of halftime with pretty solid effort, but they continue to be overwhelmed on the talent front.

Bucks 53, Heat 81 - 8:28 left in the third quarter

That stuff by Giannis is a pretty solid encapsulation who how dominant the Heat were in that first half. They got whatever they wanted on offense and didn't have to sweat much on the other end.

Bam led the way with 21 points on 6-of-10 shooting, Giannis had 10 points, 10 rebounds and five assists, and Klay Thompson and Ryan Conwell combined for six threes.

For the Bucks, Brayden Burries (eight points on 2-of-3 shooting) had some nice moments (the block above aside) and Kyle Kuzma had 14 points.

Analysis of this game has understandably shifted, almost primarily to look of Miami's jerseys and floor.

The Heat are crushing the Bucks. And barring a miracle, the result is pretty much assured.

Bucks 42, Heat 66 - 3:23 left in the second quarter

Bam is clearly taking this game personally. He's playing with a ton of energy and already has 19 points in 14 minutes.

This game could be all but over by halftime.

Bucks 33, Heat 51 - 6:50 left in the second quarter

Regardless of who's on the floor, Milwaukee can't stop the Heat on that end of the floor, but at least the players with something to prove are bringing effort.

Burries is up to eight points in 10 minutes after the buckets above.

Bucks 28, Heat 44 - 8:52 left in the second quarter

The Bucks would almost certainly be in better shape in both the short and long term if they'd just swap the young guys into the vets' spots in the rotation, but they must be very serious about boosting trade value (even though more exposure of Kuzma and Turner probably hurts that).

The reserves played with a lot more energy than most of the starters, and Milwaukee is unsurprisingly in a double-digit hole after one.

Bucks 23, Heat 34 - 12:00 left in the second quarter

This is a little surprising. Herro had some great years with the Heat and didn't ask to be traded.

Maybe the acrimony stems from this summer's dust-up between Bam and Herro, and Herro's now feeding into it by snarling at the crowd.

But this wasn't something I was expecting coming into tonight.

Bucks 20, Heat 28 - 2:49 left in the first quarter

The Bucks have had a couple nice possessions. They're clearly playing with some passion in this revenge game. Their last bucket was preceded by four offensive rebounds.

But there's a pretty significant talent gap on display here. And Milwaukee simply doesn't have any good answers for Giannis (seven rebounds and four assists already) and Bam (eight points). Klay Thompson's (10 points and three threes) shooting is going to be a huge problem, too.

Bucks 20, Heat 28 - 2:51 left in the first quarter

There was plenty of bad blood between Bam and Herro after this past summer's trade, to the point that Adebayo swung at him during summer league action.

Now, they're exchanging baskets early in this one (and Herro is already snarling at the Heat fans).

Bucks 7, Heat 11 - 7:35 left in the first quarter

Two players who made names for themselves in Miami now have a shot at a little revenge tonight.

Bucks 1, Heat 5 - 10:11 left in the first quarter

Right now, the plan is for the Heat to only use this "Vice City" court for one game, but it looks incredible.

And I'm thinking, if the response is strong enough and GTA 6 captures the world's collective imagination for long enough, that plan could change.

Outside of an effort to juice their trade value, it's hard to fathom reasons why Milwaukee is starting veterans like Kyle Kuzma and Jericho Sims over Jaquez and Ware.

On the bright side, Brayden Burries is where he should be now. The Bucks need to give him as much developmental runway as possible.

Tonight isn't just Giannis' first game against the Bucks and Herro, Jaquez, Ware and Jakučionis' first game back in Miami, it's the last Miami home game before the much anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

With "Vice City" being modeled after Miami, embracing the connection was a no-brainer for the Heat organization.

The Miami Heat gave up all of Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez, Kel'el Ware and Kasparas Jakučionis in the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade.

This is their first chance at a "revenge game." And while the 1-13 Bucks are almost certainly going to lose, at least a couple of them might be able to prove a point.

Herro and Jaquez lead the Bucks in wins over replacement player and points per game. And they're first and fourth, respectively, in assists per game.

After their 3-6 start, there were plenty of fans and analysts ready to hit the panic button over the new-look Miami Heat, but they're finding their rhythm now.

The Heat enter this game on a five-game winning streak. And while it's fair to take the first two, against the Sacramento Kings and Utah Jazz, with a grain of salt, the rest of the run includes wins over the Cleveland Cavaliers, Detroit Pistons and Houston Rockets.

And during these five games, Miami has several players cooking. Giannis Antetokounmpo is averaging 30.0 points, 12.2 rebounds and 4.6 assists, Klay Thompson is adding 19.3 points and shooting 47.6 percent from three, Bam Adebayo is at 18.0 points, 7.2 rebounds and 3.4 assists and Davion Mitchell is putting up 17.8 points and 11.0 assists.

This team suddenly looks like the contender many expected it to be. And that's unlikely to change against Giannis' former team on Wednesday.

Milwaukee has a handful of interesting young (or at least youngish) players on the roster, but they haven't jelled into anything resembling a winning basketball team.

They're one of two one-win teams left in the NBA this season, and they have a worse winning percentage than the other one (the Sacramento Kings).

And given their struggles, the sooner they can unload veterans like Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner, and give even more time an opportunity to up-and-comers like Brayden Burries, the better.

articles.title: Bold Trade Proposal Sends Suns' Devin Booker to Eastern Conference Contender
articles.summary: The never-ending trade discussions surrounding Devin Booker continue.
articles.body:
Devin Booker has never given any indication that he would ever be open to departing the Phoenix Suns .

As a matter of fact, it seems that both sides are fully content with moving forward as a pairing for the long-term.

This won't stop trade conversation from arising, however, with the Suns' 6-7 start not doing any favors in quieting down chatter.

Yet another Eastern Conference foe comes into the fold in a new trade proposal that would shock the entire NBA world.

Zach Buckley of Bleacher Report proposes a bold trade that would send Booker north of the border.

The Suns would send Booker, as well as Luke Kennard to Toronto in exchange for RJ Barrett, Immanuel Quickley, 2029 first-round pick, and a 2030 first-round pick swap.

This trade makes sense from Buckley's perspective due to Mat Ishbia's steadfast approach that the Suns will never truly bottom out. This deal would give Phoenix two players that can contribute right away, while also giving them an opportunity to draft building blocks in the coming years.

The Suns do this trade if two major factors become true.

These factors are simple - when Phoenix management realizes there's no realistic path towards building a title contender in the years to come, and if the organization in turn decides to do right by Booker by sending him to a title contender.

This move would be excruciating, but it would gift Booker a real chance to win an NBA title. It would also gift the Suns significantly more flexibility moving forward on the cap sheet while also proving two solid, if unspectacular, players back in return.

Phoenix should ultimately shy away from this proposal, especially if Booker prefers to remain a member of the franchise.

Financial flexibility and draft capital matter, but the roster that GM Brian Gregory has crafted deserves time to develop as a unit. Gregory has also earned the right to be staunch in a steep asking price when it comes to any possible trade conversations around Booker.

There's little doubt that the Suns would be met with copious amounts of interest from the rest of the association, which would inherently drive up trade value.

Ultimately, there's little incentive to give up on the franchise's all-time leading scorer at this current time.

articles.title: Houston knocks off top-ranked Florida to reach Players Era 8 championship
articles.summary: Houston will now wait for either Kansas or West Virginia in the Players Era 8 championship game.
articles.body:
No. 8 Houston surged ahead in the second half to knock off No. 1 Florida 86-76 on Wednesday afternoon at Michelob Ultra Arena. It marked the first time the two programs had squared off since Florida beat Houston to claim the national championship two seasons ago.

The win pushed the Cougars into the Players Era 8 championship game, where they'll await either No. 11 Kansas or West Virginia on Thursday night. The Gators, meanwhile, will head home with their first loss of the season, a defeat that will likely pave the way for a new team to claim the top spot in the national poll Monday.

This is the second straight win for Houston over a No. 1-ranked team. The Cougars also beat then-top-ranked Duke in the 2025 Final Four to reach the championship game.

After a back-and-forth first half, Houston came out of the locker room surging. The Cougars used an 11-0 run early in the second period to take a 10-point lead, their largest of the afternoon, capped by a tip-in from Chase McCarty. That was part of an extended 20-7 run.

Florida didn't go away. The Gators rattled off three straight buckets, including a huge fast-break slam from Denzel Aberdeen, to get the game back within two possessions.

But Houston shut down Florida again after that, and very quickly took a double-digit lead. The Gators went nearly five full minutes without a field goal. When they finally got one to fall, Thomas responded with a perfect floater to keep Houston's lead at 14.

Houston had an answer for every push that Florida made the rest of the way, and held on to secure the 10-point win. They outscored the Gators by 13 in the second half and forced 12 turnovers compared to the six they gave up.

Aberdeen led the Gators with 25 points after he shot 9-of-13 from the field. Thomas Haugh finished with 18 points and Urban Klavzar added 14 off the bench. The Gators, who already had key wins over Miami and Florida State this fall, now sit at 5-1 on the season.

Dedan Thomas Jr. dropped a career-high 30 points for the Cougars while shooting 10-of-17 from the field. Joseph Tugler added 14 points and 10 rebounds, and Mercy Miller finished with 13 points. The Cougars went just 3-of-9 from the 3-point line.

Head coach Kelvin Sampson is in his 13th season with the Cougars, and he's turned the program into a powerhouse. Houston has been to at least the second weekend of the NCAA tournament in all but one of Sampson's eight trips to the Big Dance, and the Cougars came close to claiming the university's first national championship two seasons ago.

While they are a long way from pulling that off this season, Sampson already has a signature win under his belt and now has the opportunity to claim an early championship on Thursday night. That's about as good of a start to the 2026-27 season as Sampson could have asked for.

articles.title: Boston Celtics vs. Denver Nuggets Live NBA Updates, Scores and Highlights
articles.summary: A game that started sleepy for the Denver Nuggets and sizzling for the Boston Celtics got completely flipped on its head over 48 fascinating minutes.
articles.body:
A game that started sleepy for the Denver Nuggets and sizzling for the Boston Celtics got completely flipped on its head over 48 fascinating minutes.

The Nuggets chipped away the entirety of their once 17-point deficit and rallied to swipe a 105-101 win on their home floor. Nikola Jokić netted a team-high 24 points (to go along with nine assists and eight rebounds), while Jamal Murray added 21 points, including five in the final two minutes.

Jayson Tatum led Boston with 24 points, but 20 of them came in the first half. Paul George finished with only 10 points on 11 shots before fouling it in just 23 minutes.

This was a tie game with fewer than four minutes left, and Boston twice took the lead from there. But Denver closed on an 8-2 run over the final two minutes and change to swipe a big, perhaps momentum-building win.

It's always tread-carefully territory when discussing something related to refs in front of the cameras, but Joe Mazzulla's bigger point here is right. Boston had a chance to put Denver away earlier, and it never took advantage.

The Celtics had chances to pull this out late, but they probably lost it in the third quarter. The Nuggets adjusted their pick-and-roll coverage, and it felt like Boston never got a grasp of it. Passes were forced, tight-space dribbling was sloppy and all of those giveaways fueled a Denver offense that had been stuck in the mud.

Boston won the first two quarters by six points apiece. That entire advantage was wasted when it was outscored by 12 points in the third.

Adelman is pretty spot-on here. Even reputation shooters only stress the defense so much on a night when the offense goes an abysmal 7-of-31 from three.

And, again, Denver needed every bit of DeMar DeRozan's veteran savvy, shooting touch, whistle-drawing and foul shot-making to squeak this out.

The Nuggets don't win this game without DeMar DeRozan. Full stop.

When he wasn't putting the Celtics into foul trouble, he was wiggling himself free for his trademark mid-range jumper. That throwback approach is unique in the modern game, and as Nikola Jokić relayed afterward, the Nuggets "need to learn how to play with him." Maybe this was a big step in that direction.

The Celtics weren't in a great situation when this happened, but this took them from needing a miracle make to being without a prayer.

Was it the right call? The ESPN crew seemed to think so, but you can understand Boston's frustration, too. You obviously can't decipher someone else's intent, but this felt like a frustrated player throwing the ball down court in preparation of it being advanced. The refs felt otherwise.

Does the official scorekeeper credit Murray with a win here or the save? Or both, maybe?

When Denver was in a had-to-have-it possession, Murray found himself a crease and then exploded into unguardable stepbacks for the win.

The ESPN crew mentioned quite a bit how the Nuggets lacked a signature win this season. This feels like it should qualify, even if it seemed as much of a Celtics' collapse as anything.

Still, Denver beat a really good team and played a big part in that collapse. The Nuggets bringing extra pressure to the roll man really short-circuited the Celtics' offense in the third quarter, and their offensive aggressiveness put Boston into early foul trouble in each of the final two frames.

Denver's offense sputtered a ton tonight, but when it needed a big bucket, Murray provided it. The pick-and-choose two-man game with Nikola Jokić remains one of the NBA's most powerful weapons.

The Celtics' odds of winning couldn't have been great had they trailed by three in the closing seconds, but this turned to an impossibility with the technical call on Jayson Tatum. He threw the ball toward a ref at half court. Was their intention behind it? The officials clearly thought so.

Jamal Murray made the technical free throw to push the advantage to four, and that was a wrap.

This is back-and-forth like a great tennis volley.

Back-taps, loose-ball scrambles and finally a thunderous flush. Celtics did it all on this critical possession.

If Boston Loses, It Can Blame the Foul Line

The refs have had a quick whistle at times tonight, but the Nuggets have taken better advantage of that. Boston has doubled-up Denver at the foul line with 20 free made throws to the Celtics' 10.

Score: Celtics 99, Nuggets 97 | 2:33 remaining in the fourth quarter

Look, there wasn't a lot of defensive resistance here, but you still like the read and the assertiveness from Neemias Queta. He's been active: 13 points, seven boards and three assists in 22 minutes.

Boston's big-man energizers have been invaluable tonight, and rookie Chris Cenac Jr. has played a big part in that. He has flown around defensively and flashed his play-finishing potential on offense with a hammer dunk and this fearless three.

Score: Celtics 95, Nuggets 95 | 5:04 remaining in the fourth quarter

George has been mostly awesome this season, but this was not his night. He had more shots (11) than points (10), and while he made plays defensively (three steals, one block), his aggressiveness veered into recklessness at times, and the refs took notice.

Score: Nuggets 93, Celtics 92 | 5:50 remaining in the fourth quarter

Four quick fouls again for the Celtics, and all four were drawn by DeMar DeRozan. Defending Denver's starters for a long stretch in the bonus will not be fun.

Score: Celtics 90, Nuggets 86 | 7:43 remaining in the fourth quarter

Great penetration by Derrick White here to draw the defense, and a savvy slip in to the basket for the bouncy rookie Chris Cenac Jr.

Tatum Scored First Points of Second Half in Style

Things got plenty clogged for Jayson Tatum in the half-court during the third quarter, but he went full-throttle to find an opening for his first points of the half late in the frame.

At times, it seems like Nikola Jokić might have eyes in the back of his head. Here, he put eyes on the back of the defender's head and ended up adding to his perpetually growing highlight reel of delectable dimes.

It hasn't been a masterpiece throughout for Nikola Jokić, but his stat line might look like one. He's up to 24 points and seven assists while shooting better than 50 percent from the field, hitting half of his threes and giving up a single turnover.

Score: Celtics 80, Nuggets 80 | End of the third quarter

Denver's defensive activity has ramped way up, and Boston's offense has stalled out. Jayson Tatum, who authored a 20-point first half, is awaiting his first second-half points.

Now it's Boston struggling mightily with ball control, and Denver tickling the twine. There are actual lead changes happening finally, and the teams are starting to trade blows. Buckle up!

Score: Nuggets 73, Celtics 72 | 2:10 remaining in the third quarter

Either Denver has awakened, or Boston has been lulled into sleep. Either way, things are looking sloppy for the Celtics now, and the Nuggets are taking advantage with quick-strike scores.

Score: Celtics 67, Nuggets 65 | 5:01 remaining in the third quarter

Nuggets Are a Wake-Up Away from Making This Interesting

There's a real sleepy feel to a lot of what Denver has done so far. Bad giveaways, missed rotations, settling on offense. It's almost like this game was played the day after GTA6 release day, not the night before.

But Boston hasn't hit enough shots to pull away. If the Nuggets can stop snoozing their alarm, they can slide into the driver's seat.

Score: Celtics 67, Nuggets 59 | 6:58 remaining in the third quarter

Great Selflessness, Great Find, Great Cut

Neemias Queta is making things happen as a pick-and-roll screener and not only as a finisher. He's made a few simple, slick plays off of the short roll so far.

Score: Celtics 67, Nuggets 57 | 7:25 remaining in the third quarter

Nuggets Have a Path To Third-Quarter Points

It's been a quick whistle for Boston to start. And Denver has had a few solid defensive possessions by successfully wagering that Hugo González won't punish it for leaving him unattended on the perimeter.

Bonus free throws already for the Nuggets. This score is a lot closer than the game flow has felt.

Score: Celtics 65, Nuggets 57 | 9:10 remaining in the third quarter

That hustle play to end the half felt like such a game-changer. Turns out it was at least a lineup-changer.

Chris Cenac Jr. Finding His Niche? (Or Niches?)

Those are regular rotation minutes in consecutive contests for the rookie first-rounder, and it isn't hard to see why. His blend of mobility, length and athleticism is top-notch, and even if everything feels a little sped-up around him, his explosion can help him find his footing.

While he was the only one of the 12 Celtics to see first-half minutes with a negative plus/minus (minus-3 in five minutes), that feels like a clear example of that stat's ability to mislead, especially in a tiny sample.

This sequence started with a tremendous strip of Jayson Tatum by Jamal Murray. When Christian Braun started cocking back, you could almost feel life being breathed into Ball Arena.

And then Hugo González happened. Deflating for Denver, big for Boston.

Score: Celtics 61, Nuggets 49 | End of the second quarter

While the Nuggets are half-stepping through too many defensive possessions, the Celtics are getting this kind of hustle from sophomore swingman Hugo González.

This looked certain to be the kind of highlight play that could have perked up the entire building. Instead, González wound up with a huge hustle play that was initially called a defensive foul but was overturned after a challenge, and Denver came up empty on the half's final possession.

There's a lot to nitpick (or outright criticize) with the way the Nuggets are playing, but a big chunk of this lead is just tied to Tatum doing Tatum things. He's cooking up an efficient 20-point half so far.

The way Denver is defending, its only hope might be overwhelming Boston with offense. That hasn't happened yet, but it still has to be encouraging to see Nikola Jokić getting a couple of long-range looks to fall.

Score: Celtics 61, Nuggets 44 | 1:15 remaining in the second quarter

Celtics Are Scrambling this Nuggets Defense

Denver's defense looks like a brutal combination of sluggish and spacey. The effort level just hasn't been there, and it's been glaring with the Nuggets offense struggling to find its rhythm.

Denver is veering a little uncomfortably close to danger zone here. The shots aren't falling, the focus isn't there and the defense remains a step slow.

It's not necessarily getting late early here, but the Nuggets need to find a spark somewhere.

Score: Celtics 49, Nuggets 34 | 4:44 remaining in the second quarter

Chris Cenac Jr. Getting Active on Defense

Rookies on good teams sometimes have to force their way into their role, and Cenac, this year's 27th pick, might be doing that with his defensive energy.

This is his third straight appearance, and he could become more of a rotation regular with activity like this.

While George's resurgence ranks favorably among the best early-season surprises around the Association, it hasn't showed up tonight.

He's just 1-of-7 from the field (1-of-5 from three) and might be done for the half with this foul trouble.

Score: Celtics 45, Nuggets 34 | 6:49 remaining in the second quarter

Chris Cenac Jr. bought himself some floor time, and Boston is trying out a double-big look with the rookie and Mitchell Robinson. It's a big, bouncy pairing, but the offense can get a little cramped. And the Celtics have to hit the glass to make this work.

Score: Celtics 42, Nuggets 32 | 7:35 remaining in the second quarter

Want an easy energizer? How about getting a perfect 2-of-2 trip from your 30 percent shooting rim-runner.

There is a team looking sluggish and unfocused here, and it's not the visitors. Boston is routinely turning good shots into great ones, while Denver is fumbling through possessions with nearly as many turnovers (seven, including Spencer Jones twice stepping out of bounds) as field goals (10).

Score: Celtics 38, Nuggets 26 | 10:16 remaining in the second quarter

The eye test sees he's in a groove, and the stat sheet says he's almost always grooving early.

The patience from Jayson Tatum, the effortless screen-setting by Neemias Queta and, of course, the chef's-kiss splash from Tatum.

Jayson Tatum Is Crushing His One-Man Show

No one really looked in a great flow during the first frame, other than Tatum. He just looks completely in control and confident he can get to his spots.

Score: Celtics 30, Nuggets 24 | End of the first quarter

The Celtics are making the Nuggets work on defense, and Denver hasn't always been up to the challenge. Neemias Queta is almost pinging from one pick to another.

Score: Celtics 27, Nuggets 22 | 32.2 seconds remaining in the first quarter

Threes Are Flying—and Falling for the Celtics

Boston has had some success with a few rim attacks, but otherwise it's rinse and repeat with this high-volume perimeter attack.

Turns out, this game didn't actually end within the first six minutes. Please read that in the sarcastic font with which it was written.

The Celtics are slowing down a bit, and Jamal Murray is taking advantage. He's up to a team-high seven points, and the Nuggets have needed every last one.

Score: Celtics 20, Nuggets 17 | 2:40 remaining in the first quarter

Denver Has 3 Field Goals; Mitchell Robinson Has 2 FTs

The nervous energy inside Ball Arena is coming through the speakers. It's even quiet enough for Mitchell Robinson to confidently bury a pair of free throws.

Denver's half-court offense looks choppy, but it always helps having a passing savant for a center with full-court range on his passing.

Jayson Tatum Outscoring the Nuggets So Far

Boston's defense looks disruptive, and Denver's offense looks disruptable. Jayson Tatum is cooking so far, netting 10 points on 4-of-5 shooting (2-of-3 from range).

Score: Celtics 15, Nuggets 8 | 6:09 remaining in the first quarter

Popcorn? Check. Full water bottle? Check. Unbridled excitement? CHECK!

The Nuggets are starting with their preferred opening quintet. As with most things Denver, the results have been spotty so far. The Nuggets have gone 5-4 in games started by this group.

The Celtics have rolled out this starting lineup three times so far. All three were victories, and the closest contest was a 22-point road drubbing of the Philadelphia 76ers.

Think the Celtics can clear room for Aaron Gordon's nephew on their coaching staff? Apparently, no one knows Gordon's moves any better.

Celtics Hitting the Marks of a Contender

When Boston swapped out Jaylen Brown for Paul George and draft picks this offseason, it seemingly lowered its ceiling. But zero decline has been evident yet.

The Celtics (11-3) look as dangerous as ever. And very much the part of a contender. History holds that it generally takes top-10 efficiency ranks on both ends of the floor to capture the crown. Boston, the league leader in net rating , has upped the ante as one of two teams (along with San Antonio) with top-five rankings on offense (fourth) and defense (second).

Remember when the narrative around Nikola Jokić was that he may no longer be at the peak of his powers? Well, his last four outings could be big reminders of the deception powers of a small sample.

Granted, this is a small sample, too, but here's his output from his last four contests: 26.5 points, 12.5 rebounds, 8.5 assists and 2.5 stocks with 58.3 percent shooting overall and an 89.5 percent conversion rate at the stripe. His three-ball isn't even falling yet, too.

Boston's frontcourt will have its hands full tonight.

Denver is rarely the easiest place to play. Beyond the elements, there's also that 6'11", 284-pound playmaker/three-level scorer/genius IQ-possessor to contend with.

That said, the Nuggets have had trouble defending their throne amid this rocky start. They have just a 2-3 mark on their home floor compared with a 4-2 record on the road. The Celtics will respect the challenge in front of them, but this hasn't been as daunting of a visit (so far) as it has in the past.

Launch day of Grand Theft Auto VI is here—or will be in a few hours. And shoutout to the Nuggets' social team for capitalizing on having a CJ on the roster. Think they'll be on the sticks before shut-eye? I'd put my mortgage on it.

articles.title: UNC's Cameron Fens Files Lawsuit Against NCAA, Seeking to Recover Year Hampered by Foot Injury
articles.summary: HILLSBOROUGH, N.C. (AP) — North Carolina center Cameron Fens has filed a lawsuit against the NCAA, seeking to recover a year cut short by a misdiagnosed foot injury at his previous school and play while the case is resolved.
articles.body:
HILLSBOROUGH, N.C. (AP) — North Carolina center Cameron Fens has filed a lawsuit against the NCAA, seeking to recover a year cut short by a misdiagnosed foot injury at his previous school and play while the case is resolved.

Attorneys for Fens filed the complaint Wednesday in Orange County, the district where UNC is based. Fens had previously been part of a lawsuit in Tennessee tied to the NCAA's move to a five-year eligibility model in hopes of acquiring a fifth year for this season.

He has yet to play for the Tar Heels this season. The NCAA didn't immediately respond to a request for comment from The Associated Press.

The new lawsuit centers on a stress fracture in his right foot suffered early in his third college season while playing at South Dakota. Fens' attorneys argue that the injury was misdiagnosed as a muscle or tendon injury without using imaging technology like an X-ray, and that a correct diagnosis would have cut short his season to the point that he would have qualified for a redshirt waiver from the NCAA.

Fens had sought a waiver through South Dakota with the NCAA in February, then transferred to UNC for this season. That move came at a time when college athletes from the high school class of 2022 had filed lawsuits across the country to gain access to the fifth year of eligibility that was due to start after their eligibility expired earlier this year.

The NCAA denied Fens' waiver in October, saying he was medically cleared to compete at his original school.

Fens felt pain in his foot in November 2024, but continued playing and practicing through pain before aggravating the injury in January 2025, according to the complaint.

He didn't play again, with a surgeon finding that the bone had showed signs of partial healing from a lingering fracture and that the second injury "was a progression" of the first, according to the complaint.

articles.title: No 1 Florida loses to Houston as four of the preseason AP top five fall before Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Dedan Thomas Jr. scored 30 as No. 8 Houston avenged its 2025 national title loss by beating No. 1 Florida 86-76, handing the Gators their first loss.
articles.body: Houston had waited since April 2025 for another shot at Florida. On Wednesday, the Cougars made sure this one would not be decided in the final minute. No. 8 Houston beat No. 1 Florida 86-76 in Las Vegas, advancing to the Players Era 8 championship game and handing the Gators their first loss of the season. Florida had beaten Houston 65-63 in the 2025 national championship game. Florida’s loss also means four of the preseason AP top five have already been beaten, with Duke losing twice. Florida, which was the AP preseason No. 1 and entered the game 5-0, led 40-37 at halftime. Houston took the lead early in the second half before Florida briefly regained the lead at 47-46. But Houston scored the next 11 points and never trailed again, building a lead as large as 14 points. Dedan Thomas Jr. scored 30 for the Cougars, while Joseph Tugler recorded a 12-point, 10-rebound double-double. KENTUCKY NEEDS BUZZER-BEATING THREE TO SURVIVE NORTHERN ARIZONA'S UPSET BID AT RUPP ARENA Kelvin Sampson’s Houston program entered the game ranked eighth and has been among the sport’s contenders for years. Still, beating the team that denied Houston a national title, and doing it while that team sat at No. 1, gives the Cougars a massive November resume boost. It also makes the analytics look pretty smart. The AP voters had Houston 10th in the preseason, but KenPom rated the Cougars third. After beating Florida by 10 on a neutral floor, Houston looks a lot closer to No. 3 than No. 10. Florida joins Duke, Illinois and Arizona as preseason AP top five teams that have already lost less than three weeks into the college basketball season. UConn is the lone unbeaten member of that group, at least heading into its Wednesday night visit to Arizona. Arizona was the first to fall, losing 84-75 to UCLA on opening night. The Wildcats are ranked No. 12 in this week's poll. A week later, Michigan State beat then-No. 2 Duke 79-73, while Texas Tech knocked off then-No. 3 Illinois 84-78. Illinois responded Tuesday by going into Duke and winning by 21. The Blue Devils, the preseason No. 2, have now lost twice before Thanksgiving. The Michigan State loss only dropped Duke from No. 2 to No. 5, but expect another fall for the Blue Devils when the Week 4 rankings come out on Nov. 23. Michigan State’s stay at No. 2 may be short, too. After beating Duke, the Spartans managed just 46 points in a 61-46 loss at No. 14 Tennessee on Tuesday. Unranked Memphis opened its season by beating No. 18 Iowa State 80-76. Over the weekend, LSU went to Gonzaga and beat the then-No. 14 Bulldogs 81-80 on a late shot. On Tuesday, Indiana added an 81-76 win over No. 20 Arkansas. Kentucky can be grateful it is missing from that list. articles.title: Spurs guard Dylan Harper to miss Thursday's game against Clippers after slipping on court
articles.summary: Dylan Harper slipped on a wet spot on Tuesday night, and his legs went opposite ways as he awkwardly fell to the court.
articles.body:
San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper will miss Thursday's game against the Los Angeles Clippers with "left hip soreness," the team announced.

Harper will be further evaluated Thursday to determine his status going forward, the team said.

With about a minute left in the San Antonio Spurs' 105-93 loss to the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday, Harper suddenly went down on the wing right as Stephon Castle was passing him the ball. While it looked like Harper was maybe hit in real time, a closer look revealed that he just slipped on the court, causing him to do the splits.

Harper rolled around on the court holding his groin and hip, and was clearly in a lot of pain as play continued the other direction. He eventually stood up and walked back to the locker room after play stopped and the athletic training staff came out, but Harper looked uncomfortable moving as he worked his way into the tunnel.

"It just looked like he slipped, obviously, so hoping for the best, but don't know anything yet," Spurs head coach Mitch Johnson said after the game, via the San Antonio Express-News' Tom Orsborn .

Harper did not return to the game. He finished with 20 points and four rebounds while shooting 8 of 14 from the field in the loss, which was the Spurs' third of the season and snapped their 12-game win streak.

Harper entered Tuesday's contest averaging 18.3 points, 5.5 rebounds and 4.7 assists per game this season, all of which are improvements from his rookie campaign. The Spurs selected Harper with the No. 2 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft out of Rutgers.

The Pistons rallied in the second half Tuesday night to secure the 12-point win in San Antonio. They ended the contest on a 10-3 burst and held the Spurs scoreless in the final 90 seconds.

Cade Cunningham led the way with 27 points in the win, which pushed the Pistons to 9-4 on the season. Daniss Jenkins added 25 points, and Ausar Thompson finished just shy of a triple-double with 14 points, 12 assists, 9 rebounds.

Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs with 25 points and 18 rebounds. He had two ridiculous self-alley-oop dunks in the first quarter. Devin Vassell added 12 points, and Castle finished with 10 points and seven assists.

Though it's unclear how long Harper may be sidelined because of the injury, losing him for any significant stretch will make things much more difficult for the Spurs as they try to remain at the top of the Western Conference standings.

articles.title: RJ Luis Jr. Makes Debut for No. 25 LSU vs. ULM After NBA Stint With Celtics
articles.summary: RJ Luis Jr. made his LSU debut on Wednesday night, coming off the bench for the team in the first half during a matchup against UL Monroe.
articles.body:
RJ Luis Jr. made his LSU debut on Wednesday night, coming off the bench for the team in the first half during a matchup against UL Monroe.

He ultimately recorded 11 points (on 3-of-9 shooting) and nine rebounds in 15 minutes, helping LSU pull out a 79-67 win to improve to 5-0.

Luis was added to LSU's roster on Tuesday after a legal battle involving his eligibility this season. He signed a pair of two-way contracts in the NBA following the 2024-25 season but never appeared in a regular-season game, and was attempting to return to college for another season after the NCAA adopted eligibility rules in June that allow athletes to compete for five years within a five-year window (and after a temporary restraining order allowed players like Luis to play this season).

But the SEC created rules to punish any school that rostered a player who either had previously signed an NBA contract or hadn't properly withdrawn from the NBA draft. That was countered in the courts, and a Louisiana judge ruled last week that the SEC couldn't legally punish LSU for rostering Luis.

For now, Luis is back on the court and playing basketball for LSU.

articles.title: LeBron, 76ers Outlast Magic with Jaylen, Maxey Out, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Embiid, More
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers were without Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Dean Wade on Wednesday night. It didn't matter.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers were without Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown and Dean Wade on Wednesday night. It didn't matter.

Behind the trio of Joel Embiid, LeBron James and VJ Edgecombe the Sixers pulled off a 121-116 road win against the Orlando Magic, remaining atop the Eastern Conference standings with a 13-3 record.

Here's a look at the game's key performers:

The Magic came out red hot in this contest, putting up 40 points in the first quarter behind some torrid three-point shooting from Desmond Bane. Orlando were 7-for-13 from three in the first quarter and shot 69.6 percent from the field in the frame and looked poised to pull off a blowout win.

But Philly's defense tightened up from there and the Sixers found more of an offensive rhythm, led by Embiid, James and Edgecombe.

And then there was Tacko Fall, who came off the bench as the backup center and provided a legitimate spark for the Sixers with his interior defense.

The depth of the Sixers was truly tested in this one. Alongside the absences of Maxey, Brown and Wade, the team was also without big men Adem Bona and Dom Barlow. That meant minutes for players who have generally been on the edge of the rotation and haven't played much this season, including Fall, rookie Labaron Philon Jr., Justin Edwards and Caleb Love.

The Magic (6-8), meanwhile, are going to lament a home loss against a shorthanded Philly team. Orlando shot the ball well (52 percent from the field, 19-of-38 from three) but killed their chances at the charity stripe, finishing just 9-of-17 on free throws.

In a five-point loss, that was the difference.

The Sixers are next in action on Saturday against the Milwaukee Bucks. Orlando will face the Brooklyn Nets on Friday.

articles.title: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Heat host Tyler Herro, Bucks for GTA 6-inspired 'Vice City' night
articles.summary: Wednesday's game will also be the first time that Antetokounmpo has faced the Bucks since his trade to the Heat last offseason.
articles.body:
The Miami Heat played host to the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday night. While this was already a big game — the first time Giannis Antetokounmpo is facing his former team — it carried even more meaning.

The long-awaited "GTA VI" releases nationwide on Thursday. It is arguably the most highly anticipated video game of all time, coming out 13 years after GTA V was released back in 2013.

The game, which has already received near-perfect reviews , is set to upend the world Thursda. With estimates that roughly 16 million copies of the game were pre-ordered, employers could be dealing with a lot of "sick" days ahead of the weekend.

That might sound far-fetched, but it's true. Experts are estimating businesses in the United States could lose over $1 billion in productivity due to worker absences .

"Vice City" is a fictional city from the franchise. It is not a direct replica of Miami, but it is heavily inspired by the city, while the state of "Leonida" in the video game is inspired by Florida.

The Heat's marketing department took the chance to host a "Vice City"-inspired night in honor of the game's release, and it just so happened to coincide with Anteokounmpo getting his first crack at his old team.

To celebrate the game's release, the Kaseya Center got a "Vice City" makeover with a new paint job. Music from the video game was also played throughout the arena.

The game also featured a unique halftime show for fans' entertainment. The arena even brought some of the fictional fast-food joints from the video game to the concession options for Wednesday night.

ESPN reporter Cam Wolf showed that fans lined up four hours before tipoff in the rain to get access to the "Vice City"-inspired gear that was selling in the team store.

Wolfe also added that the arena completely sold out of the gear just 90 minutes after it went on sale.

ESPN released a video package for the game.

Milwaukee traded Antetokounmpo and Bobby Portis to Miami in exchange for Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware, Kasparas Jakučionis, and five total draft picks on July 6, 2026.

Antetokounmpo totaled 27 points, 13 rebounds and 9 assists to lead the Heat to a 137-130 victory over the Bucks on Wednesday.

The Heat are 9-6, while the Bucks enter with an NBA-worst 1-14 record.

articles.title: Giannis, Heat Top Bucks in Post-Trade Revenge Game, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Bam, Herro, More
articles.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo helped lead the Miami Heat to a win over his former team on Wednesday night, taking down the Milwaukee Bucks by the final score of 137-130 at Kaseya Center.

Giannis Antetokounmpo helped lead the Miami Heat to a win over his former team on Wednesday night, taking down the Milwaukee Bucks by the final score of 137-130 at Kaseya Center.

It marked Antetokounmpo's first game against the Bucks since they traded him to the Heat in a blockbuster swap this summer.

Everything Giannis Said After Bucks Game

Miami secured the victory after entering the contest as 11.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Here's a look at how top performers including Antetokounmpo, Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro fared during the game:

The Heat set the tone early on Wednesday, opening the contest on a 17-9 run.

Miami pushed its lead to double digits midway through the first quarter and never looked back, holding a 34-23 advantage at the end of the period.

The Heat continued to dominate on both ends of the floor throughout the second, outscoring the Bucks 40-25 during the quarter.

Miami owned a commanding 74-48 edge at halftime.

The Heat led by as many as 30 points while they wrapped up the victory in the second half. The Bucks attempted to pull off an improbable comeback by outscoring Miami 44-25 in the fourth quarter, but ultimately came up short.

The Heat excelled from behind the arc during the contest, connecting on a season-high 22 three-pointers while shooting 45.8 percent on triples. Head coach Erik Spoelstra's squad also dished out 28 assists.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin’s roster fight set the stage, Will Wade just threw a grenade in LSU-SEC war with RJ Luis
articles.summary: Will Wade sent RJ Luis onto the court against Louisiana-Monroe, escalating LSU's legal war with the SEC after a judge granted the former pro an injunction.
articles.body: The LSU Tigers officially escalated the legal battle with the SEC on Wednesday night when basketball coach Will Wade sent RJ Luis Jr. off the bench and into the game against Louisiana-Monroe. Over the past five days, 19th Judicial District Court Judge William Jorden of Baton Rouge granted RJ Luis a preliminary injunction that allowed the LSU Tigers to roster the former professional athlete. This whole saga stems from the former St. John's player returning to college for another season, after already declaring for the draft following his final game at the collegiate level in March 2025. After signing a 2-way deal at the NBA level, Luis was seeking a return to college, and signed with LSU last spring. Luis went undrafted in 2025, then ended up signing a 2-way contract with the Utah Jazz. LSU LATEST BASKETBALL PROGRAM TO TAP INTO G LEAGUE RANKS, SIGNING FORMER PRO GUARD RJ LUIS JR But, there have always been rules about former professional athletes coming back to college, though that did not stop Will Wade from recruiting RJ Luis to play basketball at LSU after the head coach returned to Baton Rouge. And, for all of those that thought this was about college football, you were sorely mistaken. "I'm gonna refer to our university statement from yesterday. I'll be happy to answer any questions on how he played. "Everybody we played tonight is eligible," Will Wade said postgame. Will Wade's basketball team was always the play, not Lane Kiffin Over the past three months, LSU had already been fighting the SEC and NCAA over its rules about athletes pursuing an additional year of eligibility based upon the new guidelines that were enacted around players having five years to play five seasons of competition. This has led to the LSU athletic department having to make a decision on whether to roster two football players one day before the Tigers faced Clemson in Baton Rouge. Ultimately, the Tigers' administration decided against officially adding the players to the roster. LSU HOLDS OFF ON ADDING PLAYERS WITH NFL TIES AS SEC LAWSUIT LOOMS OVER PROGRAM, LANE KIFFIN That did not stop the legal saga around both LSU and the SEC, after the conference was enjoined in a lawsuit filed by the football players in September that then led to commissioner Greg Sankey taking the stand inside a Baton Rouge courtroom. Fast-forward two months, and the same situation has been playing out around the basketball court pertaining to RJ Luis. "They [LSU] are hiding behind a judge, and I don't know why they think they won't ultimately find a way to punish them," one Power-four head basketball coach told OutKick. "They are actually going to fight the conference over one player and watch the world burn in the process? "I guess they are really not worried about the fallout, because this makes the whole administration look petty. No matter how you feel about the SEC, it's obvious how they [LSU] feel about [Greg] Sankey and their counterparts within the conference." articles.title: LeBron James Explains Why 76ers' Win Over Magic Might Be Team's 'Best' Amid Jaylen, Maxey Injuries
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers pulled off a 121-116 win on Wednesday night over the Orlando Magic despite being without Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers pulled off a 121-116 win on Wednesday night over the Orlando Magic despite being without Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown.

LeBron James told reporters after the game it was a test of resilience for the Sixers, especially given how well Orlando shot the ball throughout the contest.

"We weathered the storm," he said. "They kept hitting us with haymakers. Orlando, they shot the piss out of the ball tonight from the three-point line. But in that fourth quarter we just buckled down and some of those shots that they made in those first three quarters they didn't make in the fourth. And we were able to get rebounds and execute on the other end. Like I said, this is one of our better wins, if not the best win of the season so far."

Orlando indeed shot well, particularly in a first quarter that saw the Magic jump out to a 40-27 lead. They largely didn't cool down until a 19-point fourth quarter, shooting 52 percent from the field (44-of-84) and 51 percent from three (19-of-37).

Perhaps the only area of the court Orlando didn't shoot well from was the free-throw line, where they made just 9-of-17 attempts.

But the Sixers indeed kept punching back, led by the trio of James (22 points, six assists), Joel Embiid (26 points, seven assists, six rebounds, three blocks) and VJ Edgecombe (24 rebounds, eight rebounds, six assists). And on a night when Philly was without Maxey, Brown, Dean Wade, Dom Barlow and Adem Bona, they also got nice minutes from little-used rotation players like Tacko Fall (three blocks) and rookie Labaron Philon Jr. (10 points, two assists).

The Sixers are 13-3 on the season because of the immense talent they've accumulated, but they are also 13-3 on the season because they've successfully navigated games that their star players have missed. Wednesday was one of those nights, on the road against an Orlando team that brought a four-game winning streak into the contest.

There were questions about how long it might take the Sixers to jell this season, given the offseason additions of James and Brown alongside a reworked bench. Some of those questions remain, especially regarding the halfcourt offense and backup center position.

But for the most part, it's hard to imagine the new-look Sixers getting off to a much better start.

articles.title: Los Heat someten a los Bucks en el reencuentro de Antetokounmpo con sus ex

articles.summary: El griego se quedó a una asistencia del triple-doble, con 27 puntos, 13 rebotes y 9 asistencias
articles.body: Giannis Antetokounmpo salió victorioso de su primer pulso con los Milwaukee Bucks, franquicia que abandonó en verano, y guio junto a Bam Adebayo a los Miami Heat a un plácido triunfo por 137-130, el que los visitantes solo aparecieron en el último cuarto, con el marcador ya decidido. El griego, que fue seleccionado en el 'draft' de 2013 por los Bucks y lideró al equipo al campeonato de 2021, se quedó a una asistencia del triple-doble, con 27 puntos, 13 rebotes y 9 asistencias, pero fue clave para abrir el campo y que sus compañeros acribillaran desde el perímetro a los de Milwaukee. Los Heat acabaron el partido con un 50 % de acierto en tiros de campo, incluido un 45 % (22 de 48) en el triple. Adebayo, con 26 puntos, y Davion Mitchell, con 24, fueron los otros referentes de los Heat, en una noche apacible que tuvo más de celebración -en torno al lanzamiento del videojuego 'Grand Theft Auto' (GTA VI)- que de desafío. Esta noche también fue emotiva para Tyler Herro, Jaime Jáquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis y Kel'el Ware, todos ellos traspasados a los Bucks a cambio de 'Anteto', pero ninguno de ellos guardará un grato recuerdo. Herro sufrió los constantes abucheos de su antigua afición, seguramente por el encontronazo que tuvo en verano con Adebayo, después de que el base supuestamente criticara a su excompañero y este le agrediera. Herro acabó con 8 puntos y un 0 de 5 en triples. Kyle Kuzma, con 26 puntos, y Brayden Burries, con 20, fueron los más destacados en los Bucks. Reencuentros aparte, los Heat cumplieron con lo previsto desde el inicio y llegaron a vencer por 30 puntos en el último cuarto, cuando entraron los suplentes y la ventaja se redujo hasta el resultado final. Los locales nunca fueron por detrás en el marcador. Un Klay Thomson (13 puntos) muy acertado en el triple abrió una brecha que se fue hasta los 11 puntos al final del periodo (34-23) y Adebayo terminó de romper el encuentro en el segundo. El pívot anotó 9 puntos seguidos para poner el 48-28 poco después del inicio del cuarto, sin que los Bucks encontraran soluciones en ningún extremo de la cancha. Solo Kuzma, con 14 puntos al descanso, plantaba algo de batalla en unos Bucks que naufragaban en el tiro (15 de 43), lo que permitió que unos Heat mucho más efectivos se escaparan a 26 de distancia y sentenciaran el partido con toda la segunda mitad por delante. Un alley-oop espectacular que culminó Antetokounmpo, y otro mate en transición que puso la centena (100-76), fueron lo más destacado hasta el final del encuentro. La victoria mantiene a los Heat como el segundo equipo más en forma de la liga, con seis triunfos consecutivos. Son, además, cuartos en la Conferencia Este con un balance de 9 partidos ganados y 6 perdidos. Los Bucks se encuentran en el extremo opuesto. Ya suman 11 derrotas consecutivas y son el peor equipo de la liga con un solo triunfo en 15 partidos disputados. EFE hbc/hbr

articles.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo went off on his former team Wednesday night, putting up 27 points, 14 rebounds, nine assists, a steal and a block in the Miami Heat's 137-130 win over the Milwaukee Bucks.

But the Greek Freak mostly downplayed his first matchup against the Bucks:

The Heat also held a "Vice City" night on Wednesday in honor of the release of Grand Theft Auto VI , decorating the arena, court and team's jerseys to match that vibe. But Giannis didn't think the environment changed much on his end either:

The Heat acquired Antetokounmpo over the summer alongside Bobby Portis for Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware, Kasparas Jakučionis, three first-round picks, a first-round pick swap and a second-rounder. That ended what had become a yearlong drama as Giannis sought a new team after the Bucks failed to keep a championship contender around him.

It ended a 13-year run in Milwaukee that included a title and two MVP awards. It would be understandable if Wednesday's game carried a bit of extra heft. But even before the contest, Giannis suggested it was just one of 82 on the schedule.

"It's going to be just another game," he told reporters Monday. "I'm going to do the same thing. I'm going to eat the same meal. I'm going to kiss my kids before they go to bed, get ready, wake up, do my routine and get ready for the game. It's the same game. It's the same thing. It doesn't change. It doesn't matter the jersey."

Giannis vs. the Bucks wasn't the only emotionally charged reunion. There was also Bam Adebayo and Tyler Herro :

As for the actual basketball itself, Miami won its sixth straight game and moved to 9-6 on the season. After an 0-4 start, Giannis and the Heat have found a groove.

Life without him, however, has been... well, it's been bleak for the Bucks. The team is now just 1-14 on the season and lottery balls are dancing in its future.

articles.title: Heat's Giannis Antetokounmpo sniffs triple-double in first game vs. Bucks; Tyler Herro booed while Bam Adebayo stars in win
articles.summary: Antetokounmpo and Adebayo both showed out on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
More than four months after the news broke that Miami Heat big man Bam Adebayo punched Milwaukee Bucks guard Tyler Herro , Adebayo delivered another blow against Herro — this one in the form of a vindicating 21 first-half points in their first game between one another.

During a Wednesday night showdown rich with storylines, Adebayo at one point scored nine in a row and connected on a trio of 3-pointers over the opening two quarters.

Of course, all the while, Giannis Antetokounmpo was facing the team he was synonymous with for 13 seasons. And the matchup was taking place in Miami's Kaseya Center, which doubled as "Vice City" on the eve of the highly anticipated nationwide release of Grand Theft Auto VI .

Antetokounmpo played the facilitator role with nine assists and still managed 27 points in the Heat's 137-130 victory over the Bucks. Adebayo finished with 26 points. Herro, meanwhile, was booed throughout and clocked out with just eight points on 4-of-11 shooting.

Miami (9-6) has now won six consecutive games after a 3-6 start. Milwaukee (1-14), on the other hand, remains dead last in the East.

Herro is a Milwaukee native, but Miami is where he began his NBA career. In that way, Wednesday was a homecoming for him. The same could be said for Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware and Kasparas Jakučionis, who also started their NBA journeys with the Heat before being shipped off to the Bucks in the Antetokounmpo trade .

The blockbuster deal also delivered the Bucks the 13th overall pick in this year's draft — which they used to select Tennessee forward Nate Ament — as well as future draft considerations, including two more first-round picks.

In addition to Antetokounmpo, the Heat received Bobby Portis, who became a fan favorite in Milwaukee while helping the "Greek Freak" lead the franchise to its first NBA championship in 50 years back in 2021.

The end of Antetokounmpo's tenure with the Bucks was dominated by drama, particularly as the two-time league MVP and 10-time All-Star feuded with the organization over his health .

Miami gave him a fresh start , and the Antetokounmpo-piloted Heat are taking off under longtime head coach Erik Spoelstra.

Herro's Bucks are on the other end of the NBA spectrum, clearly entrenched in a Taylor Jenkins-directed rebuild. Herro heard the jeers of Miami fans over the course of the night.

Even though he won NBA Sixth Man of the Year during the 2021-22 campaign and earned All-Star recognition with the Heat in the 2024-25 season, his reputation in Miami took a hit this offseason.

Critical commentary Herro shared about Adebayo on social media led to the infamous physical altercation between the former teammates in Las Vegas ahead of Summer League action. They shared the floor together in Miami from 2019-26. In that span, the Heat made a pair of NBA Finals appearances.

But there was ostensibly no love lost by the end of that seven-season stretch. As reported in July by the Miami Herald , around that time, Herro posted a graphic on Instagram that listed the league's worst midrange shooters last season. Antetokounmpo topped that unfortunate leaderboard at 26.8%, and Adebayo came in 10th at 35.9%, per the Herald.

Plus, screenshots circulated of a direct message conversation, in which comments seemingly questioning Adebayo's play and contract were attributed to Herro online.

Herro said shortly after the dustup that he wanted to "move on" from the incident , except it was top of mind for everyone watching Wednesday's game.

Adebayo said afterward that he didn't get to talk to Herro but that he's not someone who holds grudges . He noted that he's "on to the next thing."

"I feel like I got great karma," Adebayo added, via Will Manso of WPLG Local 10 News.

Adebayo's nine straight points arrived in the second quarter. He capped that surge by stepping in front of a pass from Jaquez and turning the steal into a two-handed flush that staked Miami to a 48-28 advantage .

The Heat were in control from the jump. They went 22 of 48 from 3, including 13 of 28 in the first half. Klay Thompson continued his hot streak with four triples and 13 points.

Antetokounmpo orchestrated several of the team's 3-pointers. His dribble-drive penetration set the stage for kickouts, most notably a no-look dish that rewarded Adebayo early on.

Antetokounmpo's first points didn't come until the 5:11 mark of the first quarter. His first field goal gave the Heat their 70th point. In the process, though, he had an effect that extended far beyond his scoring.

Maybe his most impressive moment was when he rose up to deny Bucks rookie guard Brayden Burries with a two-handed rejection at the rim late in the second quarter.

In the third quarter, Antetokounmpo swung a shrewd shovel pass to Andrew Wiggins , who promptly cashed in from long range.

Then Antetokounmpo slammed home a lob from Adebayo, showing off what they can do in the two-man game.

Antetokounmpo stacked 14 rebounds and ended up an assist shy of a triple-double. He told reporters postgame that he didn't think it felt weird facing Milwaukee.

"Look, I think since I was a kid, when I play basketball, I try to lock in as much as I can," Antetokounmpo said, per The Athletic's Eric Nehm . "People that have been around me know how I operate on game days. I try not to say much. I try not to interact as much. And the only thing on my mind is, 'How can I help my team win and how can I do my job?' It doesn't matter who I play. "… I could have been playing against my four brothers and my two sons. It doesn't matter. I try to do my best and try to do the things that I've worked on and try to have fun. It doesn't matter what uniform I go against."

"Look, I think since I was a kid, when I play basketball, I try to lock in as much as I can," Antetokounmpo said, per The Athletic's Eric Nehm . "People that have been around me know how I operate on game days. I try not to say much. I try not to interact as much. And the only thing on my mind is, 'How can I help my team win and how can I do my job?' It doesn't matter who I play.

"… I could have been playing against my four brothers and my two sons. It doesn't matter. I try to do my best and try to do the things that I've worked on and try to have fun. It doesn't matter what uniform I go against."

His old team made made things look closer than they actually were down the stretch. The Bucks were paced by Kyle Kuzma (26 points), Burries (20) and Jakučionis (20).

Milwaukee is a ways from competing for a playoff spot again, whereas Miami is shaping up to be a threat in the Eastern Conference, just like the Bucks were all those years with Antetokounmpo.

The franchises are linked because of this summer's trade and what happened in its aftermath.

And on Wednesday, the Heat led by as many as 30 points, as Antetokounmpo and Adebayo flexed their value.

articles.title: Bam Adebayo Explains Not Talking to Tyler Herro in 1st Matchup Since Altercation, Heat-Bucks Trade
articles.summary: Miami Heat star Bam Adebayo confirmed that he didn't speak to Milwaukee Bucks guard and former teammate Tyler Herro during a matchup between the two teams on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Miami Heat star Bam Adebayo confirmed that he didn't speak to Milwaukee Bucks guard and former teammate Tyler Herro during a matchup between the two teams on Wednesday.

"No, I didn't get to talk to him," Adebayo told reporters after the game. "Usually I'm in a competitive mode, I don't really do a lot of talking anyway. As far as how far it goes, you see obviously the history of it. But, some of that you see how he felt. To me, I'm on to the next thing. I feel like I've got great karma. That's how I live my life, that's why I've been so blessed with the things that I've gotten."

Adebayo and Herro were teammates in Miami for seven seasons, although they were involved in an altercation this summer after the Heat dealt Herro to the Milwaukee Bucks as part of the blockbuster trade headlined by Giannis Antetokounmpo.

While the Heat secured a 137-130 win over the Bucks on Wednesday, Adebayo didn't view the contest as closure regarding his relationship with Herro.

"I've been moved past that," Adebayo said, per Anthony Chiang of the Miami Herald . "I'm not one of the people that hold grudges. Like I said, I give it to God and I move on."

Adebayo finished with 26 points, four rebounds, two assists and two steals against Milwaukee. He shot 7-of-15 from the field, including 3-of-8 from three-point territory.

Meanwhile, Herro scored eight points on 4-of-11 shooting. He also recorded four assists and one steal.

Although Adebayo and Herro were never able to capture a championship for the Heat, their shared tenure with the organization was largely successful.

They helped Miami make six playoff appearances together, which included trips to the NBA Finals in both 2020 and 2023 alongside Jimmy Butler.

With Wednesday's victory, the Heat improved to 9-6 as the Bucks dropped to 1-14.

articles.summary: Hugo González brilló en defensa con los Boston Celtics y logró su tope reboteador (6) de la temporada
articles.body: El español Hugo González jugó 16 minutos saliendo desde el banquillo en la derrota de los Boston Celtics ante los Denver Nuggets por 105-101. El ex del Real Madrid sumó 2 puntos (1 de 2 en tiros de 2 y 0 de 3 en triples), 6 rebotes (su tope de la temporada) y 1 tapón, brillando especialmente en defensa y poniéndole a Christian Braun uno de los tapones del curso en la NBA. "Limpio", comentaron los Celtics en sus redes sociales comentando el taponazo del jugador madrileño. Jayson Tatum (24 puntos), Neemias Queta (17 puntos y 10 rebotes) y Payton Pritchard (15 puntos) fueron los mejores de los Celtics. Jamal Murray anotó una canasta que ponía a los Nuggets tres puntos arriba, pero los Celtics aún tenían algo más de seis segundos para forzar la prórroga con un triple cuando Jayson Tatum recibió una técnica por lanzar el balón a un árbitro. Un gesto inexplicable de Tatum que llevó a Murray a la línea de tiros libres, donde anotó un punto que 'de facto' finiquitaba el partido. El triunfo de los Nuggets estuvo liderado por Nikola Jokic (24 puntos y 9 rebotes), Jamal Murray (21 puntos) y DeMar DeRozan (18 puntos)

articles.title: Celtics star Jayson Tatum called for technical after throwing ball toward official late in loss to Nuggets
articles.summary: Jayson Tatum threw a ball toward an official with just seconds left, which allowed the Nuggets to go up by four and seal the win.
articles.body:
Jayson Tatum got called for a technical foul at the worst time on Wednesday night, and it cost the Boston Celtics a chance at extending the game.

Tatum was called for a technical foul after he threw a ball toward an official in the final seconds of the Celtics' 105-101 loss to the Denver Nuggets at Ball Arena on Wednesday. While the act itself didn't cost the Celtics the game, it made sure they didn't have a legitimate chance to send the contest into overtime.

Denver star Jamal Murray drained a jumper with just seven seconds left in the game, which put the Nuggets up by three points at the time. Tatum caught the ball after it went through the net, and started to make a move to pass it in as the Celtics called a timeout.

But, instead of just turning to hand the ball to the official standing right next to him, Tatum turned and tossed the ball toward the official standing near the scorer's table at midcourt. The ball went behind that official, who seemed a bit confused. The official standing right next to Tatum then called him for a technical foul.

That sent Murray back to the free-throw line. He sank the extra shot, which put the Nuggets up by four and ruined any hopes the Celtics had of forcing overtime.

The throw that Tatum made wasn't egregious by any means. He didn't drill the official with the ball or seem to throw it with any malicious intent. And it even looked like the referee was looking in his direction briefly before turning his back to Tatum once the ball was in the air. Tatum tried to plead his case during the chaotic moments that followed, but the officials weren't having it.

Regardless of intent, throwing a ball at or toward an official like that is often going to result in a technical.

Murray and the Nuggets rallied from an early 15-point hole to beat the Celtics on Wednesday night. Murray had 21 points and seven rebounds in the win, which pushed the Nuggets to 8-5 on the year. Nikola Jokić finished just shy of a triple-double, with 24 points, 9 assists and 8 rebounds. The Nuggets had only 13 fouls called on them all night, compared to the 30 that Boston was hit with.

Tatum led the Celtics with 24 points and eight rebounds in the loss, though he scored only four points in the second half. Neemias Queta finished with 17 points and 10 rebounds. The loss marked the second straight for the Celtics and dropped them to 11-4 on the season.

articles.title: Los Lakers caen a la décima en pleno calentón de Doncic: "Esto es inaceptable por mi parte"
articles.standfirst: Luka Doncic metió 29 puntos (2 de 12 en triples) y se quedó por debajo de los 30 puntos por primera vez en 11 partido
articles.summary: Luka Doncic metió 29 puntos (2 de 12 en triples) y se quedó por debajo de los 30 puntos por primera vez en 11 partido
articles.body: Los Angeles Lakers rompieron su racha de nueve victorias consecutivas tras sufrir una derrota por 97-109 ante los Utah Jazz. Luka Doncic, que tuvo un calentón con los árbitros en el descanso, no pudo rescatar a sus Lakers a pesar de sumar 29 puntos (2 de 12 en triples), 5 rebotes, 7 asistencias y 2 robos que empañó con 9 pérdidas de balón. El ex del Real Madrid bajó de los 30 puntos por primera vez en 11 partidos. Quentin Grimes, que venía de anotar 47 puntos con 10 triples, se quedó en 20 puntos con 4 de 10 en triples. "Honestamente, tengo que hacerlo mucho mejor que esto. Esto es inaceptable de mi parte. Tengo que liderar al equipo de mejores maneras… Tiros y pérdidas. Ofensivamente tengo que liderar al equipo de mejores maneras", reconoció Doncic tras el partido. Walker Kessler (10 puntos y 11 rebotes) y Collin Sexton (12 puntos) fueron los otros jugadores de los Lakers con dobles dígitos. Keyonte George (30 puntos y 10 asistencias), Ace Bailey (19 puntos) y Svi Mykhailiuk (15 puntos) lideraron el triunfo de los Jazz. Doncic se encaró con la árbitra después de que le pitara otra falta técnica a los Lakers en el tercer cuarto: "¡Esto no va de ti!" "Es que no sabes cuándo parar", le replicó la arbitra. "Es muy mala...", se quejó el esloveno.

El Baskonia llega a esta cita en una situación delicada.
